separationRule: Only Nim's narration, scene-setting, commentary, questions, and interviewer statements support voice claims. Quoted answers were used solely to describe how Nim selects, frames, introduces, interrupts, and responds to them. Headlines, subtitles, captions, and publisher tags are treated as weak evidence or house convention.

measurements.name: Narration sentence length
measurements.method: Narration only: frontmatter, archival footer, captions, bold prompts, and paragraphs opening with a quotation mark removed; quoted spans of 15+ characters inside mixed paragraphs stripped; sentences split on terminal punctuation; words are whitespace tokens of Hebrew text. 49 solo pieces; W106 excluded.

results.narrationLongerThanQuotedSpeech: 36 of 41 pieces with both (exceptions W007, W062, W080, W116, W122)

measurements.caveat: Hebrew prefixes make word counts lower than English equivalents; do not convert into English targets. The split heuristic undercounts sentences ending inside quotation marks.

measurements.name: Parenthetical asides
measurements.method: Count of opening parentheses in narration per 100 narration words, same corpus as M1.

measurements.name: Interviewer prompts
measurements.method: Bold paragraphs in article.he.md that are not bylines or closing notes, across the 36 solo pieces that contain prompts.

limitations: One solo review (W114) and one coauthored review (W106).
No English originals, blog posts, academic prose, or professional correspondence in the corpus.
Seven pieces are online editions of longer print versions (W035, W108, W116, W126, W163, W164, W176).
Headline and subtitle authorship is uncertain.
2017 At and 2019 Israel Hayom periods are represented by two pieces each.
The earlier AI-generated English draft of W046 was not used as evidence.
